predecessors.name: Emirate of Diriyah
predecessors.text: Najd, where the Al Saud returned in 1824 'after the fall of the First Saudi state in 1818'

predecessors.name: Muhammad Ali dynasty
predecessors.text: Riyadh, retaken from the Ottoman-Egyptian forces in 1824

successors.name: Emirate of Jabal Shammar
successors.text: Riyadh, Najd and Qassim, taken by the Rashidis of Ha'il after the Battle of Mulayda (21 January 1891)

ledger.x: 1824: Turki bin Abdullah retakes Riyadh and founds the Second Saudi State.
1825: Turki's authority spreads over the Riyadh province.
1830: Hasa comes under Najd.
1836: Ha'il becomes a Saudi vassal emirate under Abdullah bin Rashid.
1837: Muhammad Ali's army occupies Najd.
April 1840: the Egyptian army is recalled from Najd.
1843: Faisal returns to Riyadh and recognises Ottoman suzerainty.
1847: Bahrain pays tribute to Faisal.
1848: Ha'il becomes sovereign.
June 1851: Faisal takes Qatar after Mesaimeer.
25 July 1851: the peace of Mesaimeer.
1853: Cliopatria's shape doubles.
1865: Bahrain's tribute lapses with Faisal's death.
1866: the outer desert falls away.
1871: the Ottomans take al-Hasa.
1873: Cliopatria's shape shrinks to Najd and Qassim.
1877: most of Qassim passes to the Rashidis' shape.
1885: a further fringe leaves the Saudi shape; the pages opened date none of Muhammad bin Rashid's advances before 1887.
1887: Muhammad bin Rashid annexes Najd.
1890: the shape falls to about 114,000 km2 in Cliopatria's drawing (the Riyadh and Hasa fringes); no page dates it.
January 1891: the nominal Ottoman suzerainty lapses with the state.
January 1891: the Rashidi occupation turns into annexation.
21 January 1891: the Second Saudi State ends at Mulayda.

wars.name: Expedition to Najd (1836)
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory then withdrawal: Mehmet Ali occupied Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif, Faisal was defeated and taken to Cairo in 1838, and most of the army was recalled in April 1840.

wars.name: Battle of Mesaimeer
wars.outcome: Saudi victory on 2-4 June 1851 near Mesaimeer; Faisal held Qatar briefly and the 25 July peace returned Al Bidda Fort against 4,000 German krones a year as zakat.

wars.name: Saudi war of succession (Abdullah and Saud)
wars.outcome: Saud defeated at Mutala 1866-67, Abdullah fled Riyadh and Saud proclaimed himself Imam in May 1871; Saud ruled again 1873-75; the infighting among Faisal's four sons 'eventually destroyed the state'.

wars.name: Ottoman occupation of al-Hasa
wars.outcome: The Ottomans took al-Hasa in 1871 (Midhat Pasha) and held it until the Saudis took it back in 1913.

wars.name: Faisal's attacks on Bahrain, Oman and the Trucial States
wars.outcome: No gains: three failed tries at Bahrain (1847, 1851 and a later one), failure to take Oman in the 1850s and attacks on the Trucial States in the 1860s that 'the British forces militarily stopped'.

wars.name: Battle of Mulayda
wars.outcome: Decisive Rashidi victory on 21 January 1891, the 'last major battle during the period of the Second Saudi State'; the Al Saud fled.

certainty.note: Every frontier of the Najdi emirate is a tribal or desert limit with no survey: Qassim and Ha'il are nominal at times, the Gulf coast is tribute rather than territory, and the Hasa and Rub' al Khali limits are approximate.
